scope: Proposition 7.10 (Positive-gap cutoffs) of the manuscript “Microscopic jamming in the negative spherical perceptron” (preprints/Microscopic-jamming-in-the-negative-spherical-perceptron-September-24-2026/Microscopic-jamming-in-the-negative-spherical-perceptron-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 222 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8d94e973e689e60b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 67. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Constants c, C, u0 > 0, independent of the density, exist such that, for 0 < δ < u < 1, GN,β,α(δ, u) ≥ c(u − δ). For every fixed UNSAT density in the interval under consideration and every 0 < u < u0, lim sup β→∞ lim sup N→∞ E * 1 M M X i=1 1{0<hi≤u} + ≤ C | log u| (7.16) with the same constants C, u0 at every such density. In particular every subsequential endpoint law in (7.5) satisfies the direct bound P(0 < h∗ ≤ u) ≤ C/| log u|. The same estimate bounds the ordered zero-temperature and density limsups of GN,β,α(δ, u), uniformly in 0 < δ < u. The upper bound requires no identification of positive gap tests at exact ground minimizers.
